questions.question: A statement is given followed by two conclusions. Find which conclusion is TRUE based on the given statement. Statement: M >= N ; P = Q >= R ; S >= Q < T ; N >= P Conclusions: I: P <= R II: M >= S ?
questions.questionHtml: A statement is given followed by two conclusions. Find which conclusion is TRUE based on the given statement. Statement: M >= N ; P = Q >= R ; S >= Q < T ; N >= P Conclusions: I: P <= R II: M >= S ?
questions.solution:
Statement:

M >= N 

P = Q >= R 

S >= Q < T 

N >= P

Conclusion: 

I: P <= R → False (As P = Q >= R. so, P <= R is definitely false).

II: M >= S → False (As M >= N >= P = Q = < S. There is no definite relation between M and S. so, it is false)

Neither I nor II is True.

Hence, the correct answer is “Option 4”.

questions.question: Read the following statement carefully and identify the conclusion that follows. Statement: All employees must attend the mandatory safety workshop. Conclusion I: Employees who do not attend the workshop are in violation of company policy. Conclusion II: Safety workshops help in reducing workplace accidents. ?
questions.questionHtml:
Read the following statement carefully and identify the conclusion that follows.

Statement: All employees must attend the mandatory safety workshop.

Conclusion I: Employees who do not attend the workshop are in violation of company policy.

Conclusion II: Safety workshops help in reducing workplace accidents. ?
questions.solution:
Statement: All employees must attend the mandatory safety workshop.

Conclusion I: Employees who do not attend the workshop are in violation of company policy → Follow (If a workshop is "mandatory" for "all employees," it is by definition a rule or policy. Failing to meet a mandatory requirement constitutes a violation of that rule. Therefore, this conclusion is a direct logical consequence of the statement).

Conclusion II: Safety workshops help in reducing workplace accidents → Does not follow (While this is likely true in the real world, the statement provided only discusses the requirement to attend. It says nothing about the effectiveness of the workshop or its impact on accident rates).

Here, only conclusion I follow.

Hence, the correct answer is “Option 1”.

questions.question: Instruction: Identify the assumptions that must hold for the statement to be valid, then choose the correct option. Statement: To improve air quality in the city center, the local council should subsidize electric vehicle purchases, even if it impacts the annual budget. Assumptions: I. Subsidizing electric vehicles will lead to better air quality. II. The cost of subsidies is currently high for the local council. III. Citizens are interested in switching to electric vehicles if financial incentives are provided. ?
questions.questionHtml:
Instruction: Identify the assumptions that must hold for the statement to be valid, then choose the correct option.

Statement: To improve air quality in the city center, the local council should subsidize electric vehicle purchases, even if it impacts the annual budget.

Assumptions:

I. Subsidizing electric vehicles will lead to better air quality.

II. The cost of subsidies is currently high for the local council.

III. Citizens are interested in switching to electric vehicles if financial incentives are provided. ?

options.text: Only I and III are implicit
options.html: Only I and III are implicit

options.text: Only II and III are implicit
options.html: Only II and III are implicit

options.text: All I, II and III are implicit
options.html: All I, II and III are implicit

questions.solution:
Statement: To improve air quality in the city center, the local council should subsidize electric vehicle purchases, even if it impacts the annual budget.

Assumptions:

I. Subsidizing electric vehicles will lead to better air quality → Implicit

If subsidizing EVs had no impact on air quality, the council's stated reason for the policy would be logically void. The statement assumes that more EVs on the road directly correlates to cleaner air.

II. The cost of subsidies is currently high for the local council → Not implicit

The statement mentions a budget impact ("even if it impacts the annual budget"), but it doesn't require the cost to be "high." The argument holds whether the cost is small or large, as long as the council is willing to prioritize air quality over the budget. An assumption is something that must be true for the logic to work; the logic works even if the subsidy is relatively inexpensive.

III. Citizens are interested in switching to electric vehicles if financial incentives are provided → Implicit

For a subsidy to improve air quality, it must actually result in people buying EVs. If citizens are uninterested in EVs regardless of the price (due to lack of charging stations, preference for petrol, etc.), the subsidy will fail to achieve the goal. The council is assuming that financial incentives are a sufficient motivator for the public.

Only I and III are implicit.

Hence, the correct answer is “Option 1”.

questions.question: A motorboat travels 120 kilometers upstream in 6 hours and covers the same distance of 120 kilometers downstream in 4 hours. What is the speed of the boat in still water? ?
questions.questionHtml: A motorboat travels 120 kilometers upstream in 6 hours and covers the same distance of 120 kilometers downstream in 4 hours. What is the speed of the boat in still water? ?
questions.solution:
Distance upstream = 120 km

Time upstream = 6 hour

Distance downstream = 120 km

Time downstream = 4 hours

Formula Used:

Speed = Distance / Time

Speed of boat in still water = (Speed upstream + Speed downstream) / 2

Calculation:

Speed upstream = 120 km / 6 hour = 20 km/h

Speed downstream = 120 km / 4 hour = 30 km/h

Speed of boat in still water = (20 km/h + 30 km/h) / 2

Speed of boat in still water = 50 km/h / 2

Speed of boat in still water = 25 km/h

The speed of the boat in still water is 25 km/h.

questions.question: If 'x' means '-', '-' means '+', and '+' means '÷', then what is the value of: 24 + 12 x 4 - 8 = ? ?
questions.solution:
Given Equation: 24 + 12 x 4 - 8 = ?

BODMAS Rule:

Decoding the given information:

Symbol + x -
Meaning ÷ - +

Now replacing the signs from left to right using BODMAS Rule, we get:

⇒ 24 ÷ 12 - 4 + 8

⇒ 2 + 8 - 4

⇒ 10 - 4

⇒ 6

Hence, the correct option is "Option 2".
